sentences.text: The preserved type skull measures 14 cm in length, indicating the animal was of medium size.
Comparisons with related pterosaurs suggest the full skull length was between 18 and 19.6 cm.
The skull features an oval-shaped antorbital fenestra, a hole in the bone, that measures 45 mm in length and 24 mm in height.
The pear-shaped eye socket measures 34 mm in height and 32 mm in width at its widest point.
The exposed part of the brain endocast shows a large flocculus and cerebrum.
The scapula and coracoid are completely fused, measuring 67 mm and 59 mm respectively, and form a 70° angle creating a V-shaped structure.
A 2013 estimate suggests a wingspan of nearly 2 meters for Parapsicephalus.
The species was first described by Edwin Tulley Newton in 1888.
The type specimen was collected by Reverend D.W. Purdon in the 1880s.
Parapsicephalus was recognized as a distinct genus in 1919 by Gustav von Arthaber.
A specimen of Parapsicephalus was discovered in 2011 at Saltwick Bay.
A possible additional skull specimen was collected in 1994 from Altdorf, Bavaria, Germany.
The describer noted the braincase had intermediate morphology between lizards and birds, suggesting a close relationship between these groups.
The Alum Shale Member, where Parapsicephalus fossils are found, was likely deposited in an oxygen-poor, shallow-water environment.
Parapsicephalus lived alongside various marine reptiles including ichthyosaurs, plesiosaurs, and thalattosuchians in the Alum Shale locality.
The genus contains only one species, P. purdoni, which was originally classified as Scaphognathus purdoni before being moved to its own genus in 1919.
The prevailing view is that Parapsicephalus is a type of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur.
Parapsicephalus is classified within the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
While some researchers have referred Parapsicephalus to Dimorphodontia due to its skull shape, it is generally considered a rhamphorhynchid.
A 2017 analysis found little support for placing Parapsicephalus within the Dimorphodontia.
Affinities with the Rhamphorhynchidae were considered more probable than with Dimorphodontia.
Parapsicephalus, meaning "behind the head arch," is a rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the early Toarcian (Early Jurassic) found in the Whitby Alum Shale, Yorkshire, England.
Parapsicephalus lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
In 2003, researchers suggested Parapsicephalus was closer to Dorygnathus and formally renamed it Dorygnathus purdoni, though this renaming was not universally adopted.
Several phylogenies by Brian Andres and colleagues supported the hypothesis that Parapsicephalus is closely affiliated with Dimorphodon.
